content.text: Explain the Fourth Amendment framework for searches

Fourth Amendment analysis: (1) Was there a SEARCH? Government action + reasonable expectation of privacy (Katz). No REP in: open fields, abandoned property, what you expose to public, dog sniffs (place matters after Jardines). (2) Was there a WARRANT? Presumption: warrantless searches are unreasonable. Valid warrant requires: probable cause, oath/affirmation, particularity. (3) EXCEPTIONS to warrant requirement: consent, search incident to lawful arrest (Chimel wingspan), automobile exception (PC + mobility), plain view (lawfully present, immediately apparent, lawful access), exigent circumstances (hot pursuit, destruction of evidence, emergency aid), inventory searches, stop and frisk (Terry - reasonable suspicion). (4) REMEDY: exclusionary rule suppresses illegally obtained evidence and fruits of poisonous tree (exceptions: independent source, inevitable discovery, attenuation).
What criminal charges apply to estate fraud?

Estate fraud can involve multiple criminal charges: (1) THEFT/LARCENY - unlawful taking of estate assets with intent to permanently deprive. (2) FRAUD - obtaining property through false pretenses or misrepresentation; requires actual reliance. (3) EMBEZZLEMENT - lawful possession + fraudulent conversion; common for fiduciaries (executors, trustees, POA agents). (4) FORGERY - falsely making or altering a writing (wills, deeds, checks) with intent to defraud. (5) ELDER ABUSE - many states have specific statutes with enhanced penalties for crimes against elders. (6) WIRE/MAIL FRAUD (federal) - if interstate communications used. (7) UNDUE INFLUENCE - while primarily civil, extreme cases may constitute theft or exploitation. Penalties often enhanced when victim is elderly or vulnerable; federal charges possible for significant amounts or ERISA plan assets.
